newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-State says Fiat potential QMC partner.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-State says Fiat potential QMC partner.

text.p: The Queensland state government said it has identified the Fiat Spa group as a potential partner in Queensland Metal Corp Ltd's planned A$700 million magnesium plant at Gladstone in the state's north.

Economic development and trade minister Doug Slack said his department had identified Fiat "amongst others" as a possible participant and had introduced Fiat and associated company contact to QMC executives in London.

QMC announced last month it had entered joint venture arrangements with Normandy Mining Ltd and the Ford Motor Co for a A$73 million magnesium pilot plant leading to a full-scale 90,000 tonnes a year production factory.
Slack said the project would be further boosted through the attraction of a European company specialising in automobile component manufacture.
"Much of the activity has focused on the Teksid Group, the specialist metallurgical division of Fiat," Slack said.
Teksid is the world's biggest single manufacturer of aluminium components and is set to achieve the same status in magnesium, Slack said.

"The (state government's) London office is also assisting (QMC deputy chairman) Ian Howard-Smith by helping create business relationships and opportunities in Europe similar to those QMC has established in the USA," Slack said.

Slack said the government had "played an important role" in developing the relationship with Teksid, a major shareholder in Meridian Technologies Inc of Canada, presently the world's biggest supplier of magnesium motor vehicle components.
Teksid had now undertaken to negotiate a significant annual offtake of magnesium from QMC's Magmetal project as well as indicating interest in the foundry development in Gladstone, Slack said.
QMC officials were not immediately available for coment.
